territorial_scope.description: Applies to operators providing AI companions to users within New York State; no extraterritorial reach is stated.

evidence.quote: ANY PERSON WHO USES AN AI COMPANION WITHIN THE STATE

summary.short: The bill would bar operators from offering AI companion models to New York users without a protocol for suicidal ideation, self-harm and harm to others, require recurring notices that the system is not human, and allow harmed persons to sue; effective 180 days after enactment.
summary.long: The bill adds Article 47 to New York's General Business Law on AI companion models. An AI companion is a system using AI, generative AI and/or emotional recognition to simulate social human interaction, retaining prior interactions and user preferences and conversing on personal well-being; business information-only systems are excluded. Operators may not operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless it has a protocol addressing possible suicidal ideation or self-harm, and possible physical or financial harm to others, including referral to crisis services (§ 1701). Operators must notify users at the start of each interaction and at least every three hours thereafter that the companion is a computer program, not a human, unable to feel human emotion (§ 1702). Users physically injured through self-harm, or physically or financially harmed by another, due to a violation of §§ 1701 or 1702 may sue for damages and equitable relief (§ 1703). The bill sets no agency enforcement or penalty amounts and takes effect on the 180th day after becoming law.

relations.note: Adds a new article 47 (Artificial Intelligence Companion Models, §§ 1700-1704) to the General Business Law.

The numbers present are operative format or timing requirements, not thresholds: the notification interval ('at least every three hours', § 1702) and the type size ('at least sixteen point type', § 1702). The effective date ('one hundred eightieth day', § 2) is an event, not a threshold.
